# BOOK 1 OF 2: THE EMBLEMS OF FIDELITY (James Lane Allen, 1919; a comedy in letters)

Epigraph: Chesterfield on not laughing audibly. Dedication: "To the Spirit of Comedy, incomparable ally of Victory."

## Characters
- Edward Blackthorne: famous elderly English novelist, King Alfred's Wood, Warwickshire. Calls his "proboscis" a metaphor for praise-seeking. Garden has a fern bank of ferns with personal origins (Corot, Christine Nilsson, Turgenieff). Hodge is his gardener.
- Beverley Sands: rising young American novelist, Cathedral Heights, New York; Kentucky novels; age 27 in 1911. Fiancé of Tilly Snowden. Friend of Ben Doolittle.
- Benjamin (Ben) Doolittle: practical NY lawyer, 150 Broad St / later Wall St; ex-Louisville; "land-turtle"; Polly Boles's lover, later husband-to-be. Signs letters "Ben."
- Tilly Snowden: Beverley's fickle fiancée, "Slippery Elm" Apartments; the "wild rose in a snow bank"; six sisters in family; mother's suffrage-minded household; patient of Dr. Marigold; later marries Marigold (July 1912 announced).
- Polly Boles: Ben's sweetheart, Franklin Flats; loyal but deceptive; flirts with Dr. Claude Mullen; secretly marries Mullen at Jersey City City Hall, July 1912; honeymoon Ocean Grove.
- George Marigold: fashionable physician; Tilly's doctor; sails for England summer 1912.
- Claude Mullen: fashionable nerve specialist, friend of Marigold; "umbrageous" suitor of Polly.
- Rufus Kent: long-winded president of "The Great Dipper" club, called Nestor.
- Noah Chamberlain: Seminole, N.C. professor of botany, absent-minded; "Approximations to Consciousness in Plants"; dies of pneumonia after fall, 1911.
- Clara Louise Chamberlain: his daughter/secretary, "proud daughter of the Southland"; later secretary to Andy Peters; blackmails Beverley.
- Phillips & Faulds (Louisville florists), Burns & Bruce (Dunkirk, Tenn., fern collectors), Judd & Judd ("Per Q."), Andy Peters (Seminole florist).
- Hodge: stupid gardener; "Hodge is English landscape gardening in human shape"; confuses Latin fern names; resists American ferns; dies in 1911 on his birthday/natal eclipse.
- Anne Raeburn: secretary of Blackthorne.

## Part First: Events (1910–1911)
1. May 1, 1910: Blackthorne writes praising Sands's Kentucky novel (ferns, woodland scene); requests Kentucky fern root-stocks for his Warwickshire fern bank; pounds sterling offered. Story of Turgenieff ("Ferns," "That spot is all Russia").
2. May 12, 1910: Sands replies; agrees to send ferns; sends catalogues.
3. May 22, 1910: Blackthorne lists ferns (~£5 cost); Hodge described ("Asplenium filix-faemina," "Bishop's crooks"); Hodge's Latin fights; invites Sands and wife (Mrs. Sands) to visit.
4. June 3–6, 1910: Sands writes to Tilly (chaplet, wedding journey, Blackthornes invitation); Tilly replies (slippery elm, "Canaan" story, Dr. Marigold). Sands writes Ben (land-turtle, florists); Ben replies (polecat, "a chaque oiseau"). Ben and Polly exchange letters about florists, Mullen.
5. June 7–15, 1910: Sands orders ferns from Phillips & Faulds ($25 check). Sands to Blackthorne (June 15) — "peach and bough" image; wife remains unwed.
6. Diary, June 16, 1910: Sands admits the "woodland scene with ferns" never existed — based on an imagined dry spring under a sycamore, Kentucky, August, age 17.

## Part Second: 1911
7. May 1, 1911: Blackthorne accuses Sands of dishonor; "fern stood for Fidelity."
8. Sands replies coldly (May 10); tells Ben (May 13) ferns never arrived; Phillips & Faulds blame Burns & Bruce; Burns & Bruce blame Phillips & Faulds and point to Noah Chamberlain (Seminole, NC). Sands orders from Chamberlain; Chamberlain (May 29) denies being a florist; daughter Clara insults Sands, returns check.
9. June 1911: Sands and Chamberlain exchange; Chamberlain: "Stop writing to me." Clara's letter (June 8) says father could not drink tea; "I may, once in my life—".
10. June 12–15, 1911: Tilly quarrels with Sands over England trip; Sands tells Tilly the trip is off; Tilly breaks engagement. Ben and Sands talk all night; Polly and Ben "I do" dialogue; Tilly and Polly feud.
11. June 15–21, 1911: Tilly sends Marigold letters (bill; Kentucky horse; "Kentucky childhood" dolls vs. living pets; six sisters; mother's suffrage fight); she sails to summer away. Tilly to Beverley (June 21): "I love you"; to Polly: "soul of perfidy," Mullen attentions.
12. Polly and Ben: Ben proposes for next Spring (June 24); Polly "I have set the day." Ben tells Polly to send Mullen to be "furnace-man" (June 28). Mullen persists.
13. July 1911: Sands orders ferns from Judd & Judd (July 16–23; $25 check plus extra); Judd & Judd cancels earlier order; Clara's letter (July 18) returns list, says father died.
14. October 30, 1911: Sands sees steamer leave with Blackthorne ferns? Actually: Sands sees Tilly off? (Diary references: "They are gone" — ferns cancelled; "Le Génie Oblige.")
15. Anne Raeburn (Nov 30, 1911): Hodge, angry, returned a fern hamper "charges to be collected in New York"; dogs wait for Blackthorne (in Italy).
16. Dec 1911: Judd & Judd: ferns returned as ruined; Sands pays return charges; Ben's fee $50; Sands's $75 gift; Clara (Dec 25) blames Sands for father's death ("I shall always remember you"); Clara (Jan 7, 1912) asks Sands to route ferns to Andy Peters.
17. Jan 10–11, 1912: Ben and Sands on Clara; Ben's "Great Desert dryness."
18. Rufus Kent (Jan 12, 1912): Club gossip; Blackthorne's garden spot; Kent says Sands's letter is "unbridled."

## Part Third (1912)
19. May 1912: Clara pursues Sands, asks for autographed book, writes that Andy Peters is a rascal; fired; comes to NY.
20. Sands sends Clara to Ben (May 24–28); Ben's hypothetical courtroom "adventuress" dictation; Clara vanishes.
21. June 1912: Tilly reports (May 30) Beverley's strange behavior at ferns; Dr. Marigold & Mullen questions; Polly to Louisville (mother's illness, June 2).
22. Ben to Phillips & Faulds (June 4): sends roses to Polly.
23. Ben and Mullen; dictograph in Beverley's room; Dr. Marigold and Mullen confront recordings (June 5–6). Ben to Polly: Beverley alone with ferns; "Sal Blivvens" motif.
24. Ben's June 10 letter to Blackthorne (Sal Blivvens lecture, cocksure). Blackthorne's June 21 reply (Ned and Sal Blivvens; cocksure; "broken cocksure"; apologizes; invites Sands).
25. June 30 – July 1912: Hodge dies (Blackthorne's letter, "Will you, after all, send the ferns?"). Judd & Judd, Phillips & Faulds, Burns & Bruce (pitch for Chamberlain claims), Andy Peters (seedlins) write.
26. July 7, 1912: Ben announces Tilly's marriage to Marigold; Polly coming with wedding clothes. Sands's "Meditation in Verse" ("Polly comes with the wedding clothes").
27. July 10–11, 1912: Polly disappears, then marries Mullen at Jersey City City Hall.
28. Diary July 18, 1912: Tilly's wedding day; Sands's last meeting with Tilly (veil scene: "Kiss me"); butterfly migration image; Polly's "Ocean Grove"; Ben goes to Kentucky; Sands sails for England to visit Blackthorne. Final: "Emblems of Fidelity."

# BOOK 2 OF 2: OUT OF THE BLUE (Bertrand W. Sinclair, 1927 Blue Book; Gutenberg 73542)

## Characters
- Rock Holloway: young Texan ranger, long-limbed, gray Stetson, sorrel horse "Sangre," later black pony; carries .45 Colt; grew up in Texas (Austin family; sister Cecilia; mother; father dead; attended Eastern school). Has ~$2,000 savings.
- "Uncle" Bill Sayre: Fort Worth banker (Trinity Bank), Texan dialect ("yo'"); executor of Dave Snell estate.
- Dave Snell: deceased Texas cattleman (Maltese Cross, west fork of Trinity); two heirs: Alice Snell (21, yellow hair, blue eyes) and a boy (16).
- Buck Walters: range boss/co-executor, Maltese Cross; big, flashy, high-handed, poker; wants Alice; ambitious; crooked.
- Duffy family (Seventy Seven trail outfit, trail boss Elmer): Joe, Elmer, Ed, Mark. Mark Duffy killed by Rock at Clark's Ford Odeon.
- Al Kerr: small Texan cowman of the Capital K, Judith Basin on Arrow Creek; helps Rock.
- Dave Wells: Texan boss of Steering Wheel (Wagon Wheel) on Old Man River; in Fort Benton with Walters.
- Nona Parke: 21-ish, dark hair, gray eyes, proud, dominant; runs TL ranch on the Marias; father (Parke) died after horse fell; mother died at Betty's birth.
- Betty Parke: 3–4 year old, blonde, calls Rock "Doc."
- Doc Martin: TL ranch rider, Rock's double; shot from ambush ~a week earlier by Hurley (for Walters).
- Charlie Shaw: TL/Parke rider, blue-eyed, ~20, loyal to Nona, later shot.
- Mary Vieux: half-breed girl helping Nona.
- Joe Stack and Bill Hurley: hired gunmen Walters hired ($500).
- Burris boys: suspected rustlers behind Goosebill hill.

## Events in order
Chapter I (Fort Worth, April): Rock visits Sayre at Trinity Bank. Sayre hires him ($500 advance in gold; $60/month) to watch Maltese Cross and Buck Walters in Montana. Rock: "Sangre" the sorrel. Mentions "Holy" chalk on bank door.

Chapter II (Clark's Ford, Nebraska, July): Odeon dance hall. Mark Duffy bullies Al Kerr (sets him on bar); Rock shoots Mark dead in self-defense. Kerr invites Rock to Judith Basin.

Chapter III: Rock joins Steering Wheel crew (Dave Wells) in Canada near Fort MacLeod; winter at ranch; Wells's secretive cattle; Rock leaves spring 1911 near Sweet Grass Hills; sees doggies with fresh Steering Wheel brand.

Chapter IV: Rock packs mules for U.S. cavalry (Fort Assiniboine); arrives at Marias River TL ranch; finds Doc Martin dead (shot ~half hour earlier, one shot); bloody saddle; Nona Parke and Betty; Rock looks like Doc. Supper, sleeps under stars.

Chapter V: Burial at dawn under cottonwood; Rock helps; Nona hires him ($50/month). Chapter VI: Rock meets Elmer Duffy, poses as Doc Martin; Nona's "adroit." Rock kisses? (Kiss occurs later in Ch XIV.)

Chapter VII: Rock rides to Maltese Cross round-up at White Springs; meets Alice Snell (with Charlie Shaw); meets Buck Walters, who glares. Learns Alice is heir.

Chapter VIII: Charlie Shaw tells Rock of rustling rumors (Burris boys); Walters "aims to get" Doc. Rock shows Doc's blood-stained saddle to Charlie; Nona confirms Doc dead.

Chapter IX: Rock rides to Fort Benton; meets Wells and Walters in Grand Union bar; Wells: "You're Rock Holloway"; Walters: "This country ain't healthy for you no more." Threats; Walters: "I will shut your mouth ... inside of forty-eight hours."

Chapter X: Alice warns Rock that Walters and Duffy plan to hang him. Vigilante posse (~30 men) at TL. Nona stands with Rock; Rock declares identity; Charlie backs him; Walters withdraws, says Doc a rustler; Alice denounces Walters ("I hate you").

Chapter XI: Nona says Alice grieving; Rock and Nona talk ("You steal hearts"). Charlie reveals whisper that Rock is rustling. Rock and Charlie ride; ambushed in ravine; Rock's horse killed; Rock shoots Stack's partner? Rock captures Stack (Joe Stack, bound with hair macarte; Stack's partner Hurley killed).

Chapter XII: Rock tortures Stack by fire (foot on hot coals); Stack confesses: Walters paid $500 to kill Rock; Hurley shot Doc. Rock releases Stack on Maltese Cross horse. Rock's head wound (bandaged by Nona with carbolic acid).

Chapter XIII: Rock departs at dawn; kisses Nona by Sangre. Walters left with hard pills and wagon. Rock tells Charlie about hidden branding pens in the Sweet Grass. Rock goes to Billings by ferry; telegram from Sayre ("Act on your own judgment. Will back any action you take. Suspected this. Coming north, first train."). Rock goes to Kerr's Capital K; Kerr provides a dozen men.

Chapter XIV: Rock reaches Marias; meets Charlie; Charlie reveals hidden corrals at Sweet Grass; Walters with six men and five more riders.

Chapter XV: Battle at Sweet Grass (East Butte). Rock and Charlie scout hidden corrals (branding with Maltese Cross changed to Steering Wheel); Charlie shot off a bank; Rock chased by Walters's men, horse killed; Capital K riders arrive; Walters charges at Rock on coal-black white-faced horse; Rock shoots Walters dead; horse killed too; Rock injured (struck by hoof).

Chapter XVI: Captured cattle (Maltese Cross brands), cattle thieves in bunkhouse; Uncle Bill Sayre present; Rock explains scheme (Walters bought 1,200 head in Panhandle with $25,000 loan on coadministrator prospects). Sayre offers Rock management of Maltese Cross; Rock to answer tomorrow. Charlie shot but survives, sent to Benton. Elmer Duffy and Rock shake hands. Rock tells Nona he likes her; she cries: "there are two times when every woman cries... And I'm certainly not sad!"
(Transcriber's note: first published in Blue Book, July 7, 1927.)
